summary: JSON key ordering canonicalization mismatch across SDKs causing funcall duplicates
description: Customer reports repeated duplicate function/tool executions when their orchestrator (TypeScript SDK) issues a function call and the downstream webhook (Go service) confirms execution. The duplicate runs occur after automatic retries — confirmations appear to be dropped/mismatched at the Redwood platform because the confirmation payload's fingerprint does not match the idempotency key generated by the original request.
impact: Acme Health is observing duplicated patient-record enrichment jobs (side effects are non-idempotent) in production. Approx 1.7% of inbound function calls for their busiest route have executed twice in the last 24 hours, creating billing and data integrity issues. Customer has paused a subset of traffic and requests priority help.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use ts-sdk v1.12.3 to create a streamed chat that issues a function call with a nested JSON payload (objects with 3+ levels and map-like keys).
2) The TS orchestrator computes an idempotency fingerprint and sends the request to Redwood via POST /v1/chat/completions with header 'Idempotency-Key: <fingerprint>'.

3) Redwood dispatches funcall to customer webhook (Go service using go-sdk v0.9.7) and the Go service executes the side-effect, then POSTs the confirmation back to /v1/callbacks with a JSON body that includes the original function response payload and a confirmation field.

4) Observe on retry (either client retry or Redwood retry due to 200->504 transitional path) that the confirmation is not associated with the original Idempotency-Key and Redwood executes the function a second time.
5) Repro is intermittent but increases when payloads include empty arrays and when the webhook's Go runtime serializes the confirmation using encoding/json with default settings.
6) Customer attached minimal repro harness under an anonymized token and logs in their support bundle.

2026-03-10 16:05 Rajiv (SRE): Captured request/confirmation pairs from prod and saw fingerprints differ by hash suffix in ~1.6% of cases. Suspect mismatch in canonicalization used to compute fingerprint vs what webhook posts back as 'confirmed_for'.

2026-03-11 09:12 Liam (Eng): Reproduced locally with ts-sdk v1.12.3 and go-sdk v0.9.7 using customer's harness. Observed go encoding/json leaves map key order nondeterministic; ts-sdk was sorting keys before hashing by default.

2026-03-11 10:00 Customer (Acme Health): Confirmed they recently upgraded to go-sdk v0.9.7 and added a middleware that reserializes webhook confirmation using a standard encoder (no key sorting). Asked for mitigation while Redwood teams investigate.

investigation_notes: Root-cause hypothesis: mismatch between how the TS SDK canonicalizes nested JSON prior to hashing (it sorts object keys deterministically) and how customer webhook reserializes confirmation payload (Go encoding/json does not guarantee key order). The platform associates confirmations by computing a fingerprint from confirmation body; when ordering differs the computed fingerprint differs and matches fail.
Reproducer: local harness using randomized map insertion order in Go reproduced mismatch ~15/100 runs for deep-nested maps with empty arrays and nulls.
Alternate hypothesis ruled out: network truncation and header splitting were checked and not present in the sample traces.

Related SDK versions observed in traces: ts-sdk v1.12.3 (sortKeys=true), go-sdk v0.9.7 (default encoder), python-sdk v1.3.0 not implicated in initial report but later used by a subset of customer jobs.
Impact severity analysis: Because confirmations are dropped/mismatched the platform retries which causes second execution downstream. This is high-impact for non-idempotent side effects.
Temporary mitigation succeeded when customer echoed Idempotency-Key in confirmation body rather than recomputing fingerprint locally.

Platform-side quick fix: server now computes an additional confirmation lookup using raw header Idempotency-Key if present before falling back to fingerprint-of-body match. Patch deployed to prod us-east (canary) 2026-03-12 05:00 UTC; monitoring shows reduction in duplicate execs in canary zone.
Long-term fix: make canonicalization deterministic across SDKs and publish go-sdk patch to compute identical fingerprint (sort-map-keys prior to hashing) and add opt-in compatibility flags.
Test matrix: must include nested maps, arrays, nulls, and omitempty behavior across Go/TS/Python and across multiple Go encoder settings.
Linked documentation action: document recommended confirmation contract (either echo Idempotency-Key header or use deterministic canonicalization) in function-calling guides.
workaround: Customer applied a short-term middleware to include the original 'Idempotency-Key' string inside the confirmation payload as 'confirmed_for'. Recommended other customers who see this issue either echo the header in the confirmation or use a deterministic serializer in their webhook.
next_steps: 1) Push go-sdk v0.9.8 with deterministic canonicalizer used for computing idempotency fingerprint (target 2026-03-15).
2) Add server-side best-effort matching by raw header (deployed to canary already), roll to all regions after 48h of monitoring.
3) Update function-calling docs with explicit confirmation schema and sample middleware for Go/TS/Python.
4) Notify customer when go-sdk patch is published and offer hands-on validation for their production webhook.
5) Postmortem runbook item: add integration test to CI covering cross-SDK fingerprint compatibility.
